参考范文

The cartoon presents a thought-provoking contrast. In the left picture, a father lounges comfortably before the TV, shouting at his son to "study hard," while the boy looks worried; in the right picture, both father and son are reading diligently at their desks. The caption reads: "Rather than merely making demands, it is better to set an example."

The drawing conveys a universal principle in education: parents should lead by example rather than by words. All too often, adults themselves indulge in television or smartphones while scolding children for being lazy. Such double standards rarely work, because children naturally imitate what they see. A parent who reads, thinks and works hard will inspire a child far more effectively than any endless lecture. After all, actions speak louder than words.

From my perspective, this principle applies not only to family education but also to teachers, leaders and anyone in a position of influence. True education lies not in what we say, but in what we do. Only when we become the people we want our children to be can we expect them to follow.

这幅画传达了教育中一条普适原则：父母应以身作则，而非仅以言教。太多成年人自己沉迷电视或手机，却责怪孩子懒惰。这种双重标准很少奏效，因为孩子天然会模仿所见。一个爱读书、勤思考、肯努力的父母，远比任何喋喋不休的说教更能激励孩子。毕竟，身教重于言教。

在我看来，这一原则不仅适用于家庭教育，也适用于教师、领导者以及任何具有影响力的人。真正的教育不在于我们说了什么，而在于我们做了什么。唯有当我们自己成为希望孩子成为的人，才能期待他们追随。

France, which prides itself as the global innovator of fashion, has decided its fashion industry has lost an absolute right to define physical beauty for women. Its lawmakers gave preliminary approval last week to a law that would make it a crime to employ ultra-thin models on runways. The parliament also agreed to ban websites that "incite excessive thinness" by promoting extreme dieting.

以全球时尚创新者自居的法国，已认定其时尚业已丧失了为女性定义形体美的绝对权利。其立法者上周初步批准了一项法律，将在T台上雇用超瘦模特定为犯罪。议会还同意取缔那些通过推广极端节食来"煽动过度消瘦"的网站。

Such measures have a couple of uplifting motives. They suggest beauty should not be defined by looks that end up impinging on health. That's a start. And the ban on ultra-thin models seems to go beyond protecting models from starving themselves to death—as some have done. It tells the fashion industry that it must take responsibility for the signal it sends women, especially teenage girls, about the social tape-measure they must use to determine their individual worth.

这些措施有几个令人振奋的动机。它们表明，美不应以最终损害健康的外表来定义。这仅仅是个开始。禁止超瘦模特似乎不仅是在保护模特免于饿死——确实有人这样做过。它还告诉时尚业，必须为其传递给女性、尤其是少女的信号负责，这个信号关乎她们用什么社会标尺来衡量自己的个人价值。

The bans, if fully enforced, would suggest to women (and many men) that they should not let others be arbiters of their beauty. And perhaps faintly, they hint that people should look to intangible qualities like character and intellect rather than dieting their way to size zero or wasp-waist physiques.

这些禁令若得到全面实施，将向女性（以及许多男性）表明：她们不应让别人来评判自己的美。或许还隐约暗示，人们应看重品格、才智等无形品质，而不是靠节食达到零码或蜂腰身材。

The French measures, however, rely too much on severe punishment to change a culture that still regards beauty as skin-deep—and bone-showing. Under the law, using a fashion model that does not meet a government-defined index of body mass could result in a $85,000 fine and six months in prison.

然而，法国的措施过于依赖严厉惩罚来改变一种仍然把美视为"肤浅——而且要露出骨头"的文化。根据该法律，雇用不符合政府规定体重指数的时装模特，可能面临8.5万美元罚款和六个月监禁。

The fashion industry knows it has an inherent problem in focusing on material adornment and idealized body types. In Denmark, the United States, and a few other countries, it is trying to set voluntary standards for models and fashion images that rely more on peer pressure for enforcement.

时尚业知道，它在注重物质装饰和理想化体型方面存在固有问题。在丹麦、美国和其他一些国家，时尚业正试图为模特和时尚形象制定自愿标准，更多依靠同侪压力来执行。

In contrast to France's actions, Denmark's fashion industry agreed last month on rules and sanctions regarding the age, health, and other characteristics of models. The newly revised Danish Fashion Ethical Charter clearly states: "We are aware of and take responsibility for the impact the fashion industry has on body ideals, especially on young people." The charter's main tool of enforcement is to deny access for designers and modeling agencies to Copenhagen Fashion Week (CFW), which is run by the Danish Fashion Institute. But in general it relies on a name-and-shame method of compliance.

与法国的行动形成对比，丹麦时尚业上月就模特年龄、健康及其他特征的规定和制裁达成一致。新修订的《丹麦时尚道德宪章》明确写道："我们意识到时尚业对身材理想的影响，尤其是对年轻人的影响，并为此负责。"宪章的主要执行工具是拒绝设计师和模特经纪机构参加由丹麦时装协会主办的哥本哈根时装周（CFW）。但总体上它依靠的是"点名羞辱"的合规方式。

Relying on ethical persuasion rather than law to address the misuse of body ideals may be the best step. Even better would be to help elevate notions of beauty beyond the material standards of a particular industry.

依靠道德劝导而非法律来解决对身材理想的滥用，或许是最好的一步。更好的做法是帮助将美的观念提升到超越某一行业物质标准的层次。

A century ago Octavia Hill launched the National Trust not to rescue stylish houses but to save "the beauty of natural places for everyone forever." At the next election none of the big parties seem likely to endorse this sentiment. The Conservatives' planning reform explicitly gives rural development priority over conservation, even authorising "off-plan" building where local people might object. The concept of sustainable development has been defined as profitable. Labour likewise wants to discontinue local planning where councils oppose development. The Liberal Democrats are silent. Only Ukip, sensing its chance, has sided with those pleading for a more considered approach to using green land. Its Campaign to Protect Rural England struck terror into many local Conservative parties.

在下届大选中，似乎没有哪个大党会支持这种情感。保守党的规划改革明确把乡村开发置于保护之上，甚至在当地人可能反对的地方批准"期房"建设。可持续发展的概念已被定义为有利可图。工党同样想取消地方议会反对开发的规划。自由民主党保持沉默。只有独立党嗅到了机会，站到了那些呼吁更审慎使用绿地的人一边。它的"保护英格兰乡村运动"令许多地方保守党胆战心惊。

The sensible place to build new houses, factories and offices is where people are, in cities and towns where infrastructure is in place. The London agents Stirling Ackroyd recently identified enough sites for half a million houses in the London area alone, with no intrusion on green belt. What is true of London is even truer of the provinces.

建造新住宅、工厂和办公楼的合理地点是有人的地方，在基础设施已经完备的城镇。伦敦中介Stirling Ackroyd最近仅在伦敦地区就找到了足够建造50万套住宅的地块，且不侵占绿化带。伦敦如此，各郡更是如此。

The idea that "housing crisis" equals "concreted meadows" is pure lobby talk. The issue is not the need for more houses but, as always, where to put them. Under lobby pressure, George Osborne favours rural new-build against urban renovation and renewal. He favours out-of-town shopping sites against high streets. This is not a free market but a biased one. Rural towns and villages have grown and will always grow. They do so best where building sticks to their edges and respects their character. There is no doubt of the alternative—the corrupted landscapes of southern Portugal, Spain or Ireland. Second, customers may be willing to buy a company's products as an indirect way to donate to the good causes it helps. And third, through a more diffuse "halo effect," whereby its good deeds earn it greater consideration from consumers and others.

"I would raise prices and make it into more of a legacy product." 有时候这种改变终究是值得的。佩雷蒂举了Netflix停掉DVD邮寄服务、专注流媒体的例子。"这在当时被视为一个错误，"他说。结果这一步被证明是有远见的。如果佩雷蒂掌管《纽约时报》呢？"我不会选定一个年份停掉纸质版，"他说。"我会提高价格，把它做成一种更像'传承产品'的东西。" The most loyal customers would still get the product they favor, the idea goes, and they'd feel like they were helping sustain the quality of something they believe in. "So if you're overpaying for print, you could feel like you were helping," Peretti said. "Then increase it at a higher rate each year and essentially try to generate additional revenue." In other words, if you're going to make a print product, make it for the people who are already obsessed with it. Which may be what the Times is doing already. Getting the print edition seven days a week costs nearly $500 a year—more than twice as much as a digital-only subscription. 其思路是，最忠实的顾客仍会得到他们喜欢的产品，而且会觉得自己在帮助维持他们所信仰之物的品质。"所以如果你为纸质版多付了钱，你会觉得自己在帮忙，"佩雷蒂说。"然后每年以更高的幅度提价，本质上就是努力创造额外收入。"换言之，如果你要做纸质产品，就为那些已经痴迷于它的人做。而这可能正是《纽约时报》已经在做的。一周七天拿到纸质版一年要花近500美元——是纯数字订阅的两倍多。 "It's a really hard thing to do and it's a tremendous luxury that BuzzFeed doesn't have a legacy business," Peretti remarked. "But we're going to have questions like that where we have things we're doing that don't make sense when the market changes and the world changes. In those situations, it's better to be more aggressive than less aggressive." "这是一件非常难做到的事，而BuzzFeed没有传统业务是一种巨大的奢侈，"佩雷蒂说。"但我们也会遇到类似问题：当市场和世界变化时，我们所做的一些事就不再合理。在那种情况下，更激进一些总比不够激进修好。"
